title: 别云中手札第四十章 秦伯之死
content_zh:
那本手札，江砚贴身藏好了。
藏在棉袄最里头，靠着心口的位置。隔着那层洗得发硬的布，他能感觉到那兽皮封皮的硬实，和那道焦痕硌人的棱角。一夜下来，那点硌人的感觉，竟成了他唯一觉得踏实的东西。
天大亮了。
乱葬岗不能再留。苏挽说得对，卫家的人翻完了破庙，下一步，多半就该把这一带的荒坡野岗，都犁一遍。
“走吧。”苏挽利落地收拾停当，把那只旧药箱也替他背上了，“先出城。出了云中城地界，卫家的手，一时半会儿伸不了那么长。”
江砚最后看了一眼秦伯的坟。
那座坟很小，很矮。坟头那块没刻字的青石，在荒岗里，毫不起眼。要不了几场雪，就再难分辨。
他没再说什么话。话昨夜已经说尽了。他只是对着那坟，深深地、深深地，弯下腰，作了一个揖。
然后转身，跟上苏挽。
出城那一段路，走得提心吊胆。
江砚的身子还虚，走几步就要喘。苏挽便放慢脚步，时不时回头看他一眼，却不催，也不扶——除非他实在站不住了，她才伸手搭一把。她知道这少年的脾性：能自己走的，他绝不肯让人架着。
云中城的城门，盘查比往日紧。城门兵一脸的横肉，盘剥着进出的流民，骂骂咧咧。
江砚远远看见，心就提了起来——他是“逃奴”，又是卫家正缉拿的人，这城门，怎么过？
苏挽却像是早有打算。她拐了个弯，没走正门，领着江砚，钻进城墙根一条堆满污雪和烂菜叶的窄巷。
巷子尽头，城墙下，有一处不起眼的塌口，半人来高，堆着些枯柴。
“水门旁边的塌口。”苏挽压低声音，“前几日我进城寻物，就是从这儿。守城的懒，年久失修也没人管。猫着腰，能过去。”
江砚看着她，心里头一动。
这女子，刚硬归刚硬，心思却细得很。她去而复返、只为寻一枚旧物，却把这城里城外的进出门道，摸了个透。难怪秦伯当初一见她，就说这是个“有来历、不简单”的人。
两人一前一后，猫着腰，从那塌口钻了出去。
城墙外，是一片开阔的雪原。远处，是连绵起伏、灰蒙蒙的北境群山。

江砚回头望了一眼。
云中城那高大的、灰沉沉的城墙，在他身后，沉默地立着。城头那面褪了色的、写着“胤”字的旗子，在风里，无力地耷拉着。
他在这座城里，活了大半年。
挨过打，挨过饿，写过信，记过账，被人当众羞辱过，也第一次，敢顶撞权贵。他在这座城里，遇见了秦伯，遇见了苏挽，遇见了那扇通向“一笔成真”的门。
也在这座城里，失去了秦伯。
“走吧。”苏挽的声音，把他从那一望里拽了回来，“别回头了。”
江砚收回目光。“嗯。”
他们一直走到日头偏西，才在一处背风的山坳里歇下。
这里离云中城已经有几十里。雪原尽头，那座边城，早望不见了。四下里，只有风，和雪，和远处一两声不知名的鸟叫。
苏挽寻了些干柴，生起一小堆火。火不大，却总算让这冰天雪地里，多了一点活气。
两人围着火，谁也没说话。
江砚把手伸到火上烤着，望着那跳动的火苗，心里头那个填不满的窟窿，又隐隐地疼起来。这火，让他想起从前在病坊、在小铺里，秦伯也是这么生一小堆火，烧一壶热水，戏称他“半个先生”，催他多写两个字、多记两笔账。
“接下来，你打算去哪？”苏挽忽然开口。
江砚回过神。
去哪。
他还真没仔细想过。昨夜到今晨，他满心满眼都是秦伯、是手札、是出城。这“去哪”二字，问得他一时怔住。
他想了想，慢慢地说：
“往南吧。”
“往南?”
content_en:
Jiang Yan kept the notebook close to his body.
Hidden inside the cotton-padded jacket, next to the heart. Through the layer of hardened cloth, he could feel the hardness of the animal skin cover and the sharp edges of the scorch marks. After a night, that tingling feeling became the only thing that made him feel at ease.
It's broad daylight.
Mass graves cannot remain. Su Wan was right. After the Wei family plowed through the ruined temple, the next step would probably be to plow all the barren slopes and hills in this area.
"Let's go." Su Wan packed up neatly and put the old medicine box on his back, "Leave the city first. After leaving the boundaries of Yunzhong City, the Wei family's hands won't be able to stretch that long for a while."
Jiang Yan took one last look at Uncle Qin's grave.
The tomb was very small and short. The unengraved bluestone at the head of the tomb is inconspicuous in the barren hills. Without a few snows, it would be difficult to tell the difference.
He said nothing more. All was said last night. He just faced the grave, bent deeply, deeply, and made a bow.
Then he turned around and followed Su Wan.
The walk out of the city was scary.
Jiang Yan's body was still weak and he was out of breath after walking a few steps. Su Wan slowed down and looked back at him from time to time, but she didn't urge him or help him--unless he couldn't stand anymore, she would reach out to help him. She knew this young man's temperament: if he could walk alone, he would never let anyone hold him back.
The gates of Yunzhong City are more intensively inspected than usual. The city gate soldiers had a fierce look on their faces, exploiting the refugees coming in and out, cursing and cursing.
When Jiang Yan saw him from a distance, his heart ached - he was a "fugitive slave" and someone the Wei family was arresting. How could he pass through this city gate?
Su Wan seemed to have already planned it. She turned a corner and did not go through the main entrance. She led Jiang Yan into a narrow alley at the base of the city wall that was filled with dirty snow and rotten vegetable leaves.
At the end of the alley, under the city wall, there is an inconspicuous cave, half a man high, with some dead wood piled there.
"The cave next to the water gate." Su Wan lowered his voice, "I went into the city to look for things a few days ago, and it was from here. The city guards are lazy, and it has been in disrepair for a long time, and no one cares about it. I can get through with my waist."
Jiang Yan looked at her and felt something in his heart.
This woman is hard-nosed, but very considerate. She went back and forth just to find an old thing, but she explored every doorway in and out of the city. No wonder Uncle Qin said when he saw her that she was "a person with a rich background and not a simple person".
The two of them walked forward and backward, bending their waists, and got out of the cave.
Outside the city wall is an open snowfield. In the distance are the rolling, gray northern mountains.
Jiang Yan looked back.
The tall, gray walls of Yunzhong City stood silently behind him. The faded flag with the word "Yin" written on it at the top of the city fluttered feebly in the wind.
He lived in this city for more than half a year.
I have been beaten, starved, written letters, kept accounts, and publicly humiliated. This is the first time I dare to contradict a powerful person. In this city, he met Uncle Qin, met Su Wan, and met the door leading to "One stroke comes true".
Uncle Qin was also lost in this city.
"Let's go." Su Wan's voice pulled him back from that gaze, "Don't look back."
Jiang Yan withdrew his gaze. "Yeah."
They walked until the sun turned west, then rested in a leeward mountain col.
This place is dozens of miles away from Yunzhong City. At the end of the snowfield, the border town was long gone. All around, there was only wind, snow, and one or two unknown birds chirping in the distance.
Su Wan found some dry firewood and built a small fire. The fire was not big, but it finally gave the ice and snow a little more life.
The two of them sat around the fire, and neither of them spoke.
Jiang Yan put his hand on the fire to heat it. Looking at the dancing flames, the unfilled hole in his heart began to hurt again. This fire reminded him of how Uncle Qin used to make a small fire and boil a pot of hot water in the hospital or in the shop, jokingly calling him "half a gentleman".生”，催他多写两个字、多记两笔账。
"Where do you plan to go next? "Su Wan suddenly spoke.
Jiang Yan came to his senses.
Where to go.
He really hadn't thought about it carefully.昨夜到今晨，他满心满眼都是秦伯、是手札、是出城。 The word "where to go" made him stunned for a moment.
He thought for a while and said slowly:
“Go south. "
"To the south?"
